Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

that conjunction

after verbs of saying, thinking and knowing

also say that, think that, know that, the fact that, it happens that

classical

Plin. Ep. 7.9.15: ajunt enim multum legendum esse, nōn multa
Sen. Ep. 83.4: hic quidem ait nōs eandem crisin habēre

accūsātīvus cum īnfīnītīvō

no conjunction: the subject in the accusative, the verb in the infinitive

that (he says that …)

After verbs of saying, thinking, knowing and perceiving, Latin has no word for “that”: “they say that one should read much” is ajunt multum legendum esse. The tense of the infinitive is relative to the main verb: present for the same time, perfect for before, future for after (cōgitā et illum puerum esse et tē fuisse). Lewis & Short has accūsātīvus and īnfīnītīvus as the grammarians’ words; the name of the construction is modern.

Other words

  • quod (+ indicative) — that, the fact that

    conjunction, with the indicative · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 4.1.1: grātum est utrīque nostrum quod cupis; Traupman 312

    “The fact that”: after expressions of feeling and thanks (gaudeō quod, grātum est quod), and to explain a word just used.

  • ut (+ subjunctive) — that (it happens that; I ask that)

    conjunction, with the subjunctive; negative ut nōn after fit, nē after verbs of asking · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.101: ita fit, ut ratiō praesit, appetītus obtemperet

    After fit, accidit, ēvenit, “it happens that”; after verbs of asking, urging and taking care, “that … should” (cūrā ut valeās).

  • dīcō quod (quia) … — I say that …

    quod or quia with a finite verb after a verb of saying · avoid · late Latin · Vulg. 1 Cor. 6.9: nescītis quia inīquī nōn possidēbunt? (Lewis & Short s.v. quia, “postclass.”)

    Late and Christian Latin, as in the Vulgate; classical Latin uses the accusative and infinitive.

Examples

  • ajunt enim multum legendum esse, nōn multa

    for they say that one should read much, not many thingsPlin. Ep. 7.9.15

  • hic quidem ait nōs eandem crisin habēre, quia utrīque dentēs cadunt

    he says that we are at the same stage of life, since both of us are losing our teethSen. Ep. 83.4

  • cōgitā et illum puerum esse et tē fuisse

    remember that he is a boy and that you were onePlin. Ep. 9.12.2

  • cupis post longum tempus neptem tuam mēque ūnā vidēre. grātum est utrīque nostrum quod cupis

    you want to see your granddaughter and me together after a long time; we are both glad that you want toPlin. Ep. 4.1.1

  • ita fit, ut ratiō praesit, appetītus obtemperet

    so it comes about that reason leads and appetite obeysCic. Off. 1.101

See also say, believe, so that.
